== Original post ==

'''SYCFA done RIGHT aka Fear Attracts the Fearful'''
* '''Author:''' Brian "HuntaWarya" Hunter
* '''Published:''' October 26, 2006
* '''Rating:''' 4.98
* '''Description:''' This is the dark side deck that I used in Day 3 of the 2006 World Championships. It was the only deck to go 4-0 that day, for either allegiance.

=== Strategy ===

Old concept, new decklist.  By using significantly fewer starships and/or systems than is traditional for a SYCFA/Fear deck, I was able to fit in a wider array of "red support" cards, as well as a much more resilient ground presence at the Death Star docking bay.  This deck pays for Battle Plan/Battle Order far less than the typical Fear deck is forced to put up with.

Starting Effects:

In every matchup, you will start Endor Shield to pull Merrejk, so that you can put him in the War Room to pull your systems.  In most matchups, you will start Crossfire (to pull Fear), and Dreaded Imperial Starfleet (to make your Destroyers deploy for less).  However, in matches against dedicated LS Mains decks (such as Throne Room Mains, or LS Combat) you might want to start TINT/OE.  This really frees up your options when it comes to which 3 shields you pull, when you have Sense/Alter completely taken care of.  You also won't need to worry about the Fears being Altered for good.  Against Throne Room, your 3rd effect should be the Dreaded Imperial Starfleet, to make your ships as inexpensive as possible.  Against Combat, go ahead and start Crossfire to guarantee the early Fear.  Your ships will cost more, but they give you enough activation that you should be fine.  Against Profit or WHAP you could consider starting Decree in place of Crossfire or the D.I.S, but I have no playtest data to tell me whether that's a good idea.

Rule #1:  Make an effort to not get your Star Destroyers blown up.  In other Fear decks, you can happily use a Star Destroyer as a Control.  Block a drain for a turn, and if it gets destroyed, no big deal, you've got a deck full of them.  This deck is not *as* full of them.  It is sometimes wiser to eat a drain of 1 at one of your systems than lose a Star Destroyer to block a drain and perhaps kill an enemy pilot in the process.  This is especially true if you suspect that your opponent may be running Legendary Starfighter.

Rule #2:  Overwhelmed is for specific situations only, not just any situation where you can play it.  Consider how much damage you might be able to force in a hypothetical battle, before sending that Lateral Damaged ship and his buddies to the used pile.  Also be aware that, if 3PO with Parts Showing is on the table, Overwhelmed is far better in the early game than the late game.  Don't waste an Overwhelmed on a lone HCF if they can just pop it back into hand during their activate phase.

Rule #3:  Don't forget just how monstrous Sidious is.  In some situations, it will actually be beneficial for YOU to initiate battles at the Death Star docking bay, just to knock guys out with attrition, or put 2 points of battle damage on Mace Windu.  If there is a non-permanent lightsaber there, you'll probably want to let the opponent do the battling.  Or if there are permanent sabers, but you DON'T have Wipe Them Out, you'll probably want to let the opponent do the battling.  Probably best not to initiate battles against TIGIH either.  But otherwise, sock it to 'em, especially if there should happen to be a Draw Their Fire on Table.

Rule #4:  Set up the fleet at one location, then spread when you're ready.  Don't deploy one Star Destroyer to Rendili on Turn One, then one Star Destroyer to Kiffex on Turn Two.  Build your fleet at a single system (even the Death Star, if the situation warrants it), and then spread to cover all your systems at once when you're ready.  This will minimize the LS player's ability to disrupt your setup until your fleet is in full effect.

Card Choices:

Grand Admiral Thrawn - If you draw into either Merrejk or Chiraneau, you can pull Thrawn with the Endor Shield, to give you some extra firepower at one of your systems.  Even despite your low destiny average, most LS players are reluctant to tangle with the Grand Admiral.

Imperial Decree - One use from this card against TRM can give you all the force you need to deploy the fleet.  In other matchups, this card can help defend you from the direct damage caused by Profit, WHAP, or LU (v).  In theory, this card could also protect you against damage from a podrace, Legendary Starfighter, or Advantage.

Sidious x4?? - I decided not to mess around.  I want Sidious in play.  The 6-destiny Emperor is no substitute.  With Sidious I don't have to worry about the LS getting there before I do.  3 Imperial Barriers, backed by Force Field, WTO (v), and Weapon Levitation, usually do a pretty good job of keeping Sidious on the table.  But just in case...you've got 3 more.  However, you don't run 4 copies so that you can keep putting him back out if he dies, rather, you run 4 copies just so that you'll normally have one immediately.

Lateral Damage - Makes Overwhelmed much easier to pull off.  And when combined with "They've Shut Down the Main Reactor", can spell a quick finish to a game.

Laser Cannon Battery - Primarily included so that you can shoot down the Bright Hope.  However, with tracked 5s you could hit some of the less manueverable starfighters as well, such as the potentially irritating Outrider.  This card is also what allows you to play "They've Shut Down the Main Reactor", which again, can end a game far earlier than it would end otherwise.

Luke, Luuuke - Primarily included for use against LS Combat, but can be handy against any light deck that attempts to drain you on the ground using characters. (as opposed to non-unique speeders)  You can't drain at your docking bay anyway, so the fact that Sidious cannot drain against LS Combat is really nothing new.  Sidious appears to be a non-threat to the LS player, doing nothing more for you than satisfying Battle Order.  Until this Effect is deployed on him, suddenly giving your SYCFA deck a bit of a Hidden Base flavor.  This card can certainly swing a drain race in your favor, and with 2 Accelerates to find it with it will usually make an early appearance for you.  If the LS player finds themselves without a Nabrun Leids, they will usually have to kill Sidious by any means necessary (since TINT/OE defends the card from Alter).  And each turn that those other characters are slugging it out with Sidious is another turn that they aren't draining you at other locations.

Control/SFS x3 - In matchups where you did not start TINT/OE, the 3 controls give you a measure of defense against Sense and Alter.  But if you have nothing better to do with them, you can also use them to cancel drains, or even cancel Imperial Atrocity (v), if you REALLY want that extra point of Fear damage.  Lastly, when combined with a tracked 5, (or Combat Readiness) you might be able to Set For Stun a key pilot (perhaps Dash Rendar or Wedge Antilles, RSL) and then lay the beats.

I've Lost Artoo! - Can be used for whichever sort of tech you need.  I put Ghhhk combo under the starting effect, which can be used if one of the Star Destroyers finds itself on the wrong end of a Falcon/Life Debt debacle.  Also cancels Landing Claw, and Hyper Escape.  Stops the react from the Spiral, and can even be used to cancel Nabrun Leids, to protect your Luke, Luuuke on Sidious.  I also kept Relentless Pursuit under there.  If you're facing Home One and Bright Hope, you could Lateral Damage Home One, shoot Bright Hope with the Laser Cannon Battery, make it immediately lost with Relentless Pursuit, and really give Home One the business.

Captain Bewil - Always tough to find room for this guy, when every dark deck needs so many other characters just to function.  But finally, a dark deck with only 8 characters!  Bewil makes #9, as his ability to recycle used interrupts can be enormously helpful at times.  Luke, Luuuke or Fear being sent to used pile by Alters?  Get Accelerate and get 'em back.  Opponent forgot to grab Imperial Barrier?  Get 'em back.  Opponent did grab Imperial Barrier?  Keep snatching Combat Readiness and draw a 5 for battle destiny every turn even though you're playing a deck full of 1s.  Or if you're real lucky, keep re-playing that copy of "They've Shut Down the Main Reactor" until your opponent has run out of game-saving Houjixes.

Something Special Planned For Them - Places their retrieval cards out of play, so that you don't need to pull Code Clearance Shield.  The text that makes them pay extra to move away from you can be huge against any sort of LS space swarm.  Any time they forget the text and don't save enough force, you just got a free Gravity Shadow.  Even if they only have a couple ships on table, having to pay 6 to move them away from your pursuing fleet can make it very difficult to upkeep the HCF in the late game.

Options for Card #61:

None.  I fit everything you need into 60 cards.  This deck has it all.

Deck matchups you like to see:

MWYHL, HB, TIGIH, LS Senate, RST

Deck matchups you don't like to see:

QMC, EBO and WYS Raiders

Deck matchups that could go either way:

LS Combat, WHAP, Profit

Enjoy the deck, and thanks for reading.
